title: Ordered-column information-set elimination
description:
Extend dense GF(2) row reduction with an ordered-column preference operation that selects a most-reliable independent basis without moving coding policy into `gf2-core`.

## Background

`gf2_core::alg::rref` exposes directional pivoting but cannot consume an explicit preference permutation. The reusable primitive follows the `mrb-elimination` contract and remains independent of LLR semantics.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Accepts a complete ordered column preference and returns the reduced matrix, selected information set in preference order, and rank.
- [hard] REQ-02: Rejects malformed preference permutations and handles rank-deficient, empty, and rectangular matrices deterministically.
- [hard] REQ-03: Matches existing RREF rank and row-space semantics under natural and reversed column orders.
- [hard] REQ-04: Documents purpose, failure behavior, and non-obvious complexity on the public API.

planning.outcome: Dense GF(2) elimination selects an information set from an explicit column preference and returns deterministic rank metadata.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The change extends one core algorithm surface with focused property coverage.

title: Shared LLR reliability permutation
description:
Expose one deterministic reliability permutation beside `Llr` so soft-decision algorithms share ordering and tie semantics.

## Background

ORBGRAND and Chase-Pyndiah currently sort reliability indices privately. The `reliability-permutation` contract defines the canonical finite-input boundary before OSD consumes the same convention.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Returns each input index exactly once in ascending $|\mathrm{LLR}|$ order with original index as the stable tie-break.
- [hard] REQ-02: Handles empty, singleton, repeated-magnitude, and signed-zero inputs deterministically.
- [hard] REQ-03: Enforces and documents the finite-input precondition, including behavior for NaN and infinite values.
- [hard] REQ-04: Provides public rustdoc and property coverage for permutation validity and ordering.

planning.outcome: The LLR module exposes one deterministic finite-input reliability permutation for soft-decision decoders.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The work adds one helper contract with bounded property tests.

title: Canonical reliability convention cutover
description:
Move existing soft-decision consumers onto canonical LLR reliability and hard-decision semantics, then remove superseded variants.

## Background

The shared helper replaces the private ORBGRAND and Chase-Pyndiah sorters. The deprecated zero-consumer `SoftDecisionDecoder` trait is part of the same owner-directed canonical cutover.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: ORBGRAND obtains its reliability order from the shared permutation while preserving deterministic decoding and query behavior.
- [hard] REQ-02: Chase-Pyndiah obtains its reliability order and hard decisions from canonical `Llr` helpers while preserving SISO behavior.
- [hard] REQ-03: The superseded private sorters, duplicated sign test, and dead `SoftDecisionDecoder` trait are absent from the production surface.
- [hard] REQ-04: Regression tests cover tied reliabilities and hard-decision zero semantics at both surviving consumers.

planning.outcome: ORBGRAND and Chase-Pyndiah consume canonical LLR helpers with no superseded soft-decoder abstraction.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The owner-fixed cutover covers one convention at three enumerated sites.

title: Bounded OSD test-pattern enumeration
description:
Provide the OSD-specific Hamming-weight test-pattern source with checked growth and explicit termination metadata.

## Background

OSD enumerates subsets of the information set through order $m$, with a theoretical cap $\sum_{i=0}^{m} \binom{k}{i}$. GRAND's logistic-weight iterator remains separate because it has different ordering semantics.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Enumerates each subset of weights zero through $\min(m,k)$ exactly once in a documented deterministic order.
- [hard] REQ-02: Computes the theoretical candidate cap with checked arithmetic and rejects unrepresentable configurations.
- [hard] REQ-03: Stops at configured budgets or cancellation and reports generated, tested, and termination counters without unbounded allocation.
- [hard] REQ-04: Covers $k=0$, $m=0$, $m>k$, exact-budget, and cancelled cases with property tests.

planning.outcome: OSD enumerates Hamming-weight patterns through order m with checked candidate caps and explicit termination metadata.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The iterator has one bounded combinatorial contract and focused metadata tests.

title: Published eBCH OSD curve dataset
description:
Commit a machine-readable digitization that pins the selected published eBCH OSD curve and its construction metadata without inventing a figure identifier.

## Background

The reproduction target is eBCH $(128,64)$ on BI-AWGN/BPSK with BLER versus $E_b/N_0$, OSD order 2, and order 1 as a control. Fossorier1995 is authoritative and Yue2022 supplies an independent cross-check.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Identifies the exact Fossorier1995 page, figure, series, construction, channel, metric, and OSD order represented by the digitized data.
- [hard] REQ-02: Stores auditable $E_b/N_0$ and BLER points with digitization method, precision, and provenance.
- [hard] REQ-03: Records the Yue2022 cross-check and any material construction or curve differences without silently reconciling them.
- [hard] REQ-04: Distinguishes the published order-2 series from the campaign's order-1 control so the control carries no unsupported external claim.

planning.outcome: A cited dataset pins the exact Fossorier1995 eBCH OSD curve and records a Yue2022 cross-check without invented metadata.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The task pins one published curve through a bounded research review.

title: Named eBCH(128,64) reference factory
description:
Add the named extended BCH reference constructor used by OSD conformance and campaign work.

## Background

The existing named-constructor family stops at eBCH $(64,57)$. The selected published curve data fixes the primitive polynomial and construction provenance before this factory lands.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `ExtendedBchCode::ebch_128_64()` constructs the pinned primitive BCH extension with $n=128$, $k=64$, and systematic generator form.
- [hard] REQ-02: A committed fixture pins the primitive polynomial and canonical serialized generator and parity-check matrices.
- [hard] REQ-03: Tests verify fixture identity, matrix dimensions, orthogonality, systematic encoding, and even extension parity.
- [hard] REQ-04: Public rustdoc cites the construction provenance and demonstrates the named factory workflow.

planning.outcome: The named eBCH(128,64) factory fixes polynomial and systematic-form identity against a checked fixture.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The constructor extends one established family against one pinned fixture.

title: Generator-matrix OSD decoder
description:
Implement the order-$m$ generator-matrix OSD path as the reusable soft-decision baseline for linear block codes.

## Background

The decoder is generic over `GeneratorMatrixAccess`; convolutional streaming and other codes without that surface are outside the contract. It consumes the shared reliability, ordered elimination, and bounded-pattern contracts.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Implements `SoftDecoder` for a decoder generic over `GeneratorMatrixAccess`, with $m$ configurable through `OsdConfig`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Forms the most-reliable basis, reprocesses test patterns through order $m$, and returns the deterministic minimum soft-metric hard decision.
- [hard] REQ-03: Reports rank, candidate-cap, tested-candidate, and termination metadata while respecting the configured budget.
- [hard] REQ-04: Matches exhaustive maximum-likelihood decoding on bounded small-code fixtures, including tied reliabilities and non-systematic generators.
- [hard] REQ-05: Rejects invalid LLR length, non-finite LLRs, and rank-deficient generator input according to documented public behavior.

planning.outcome: Order-m OSD implements SoftDecoder for GeneratorMatrixAccess codes with exhaustive-ML equivalence on bounded fixtures.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The decoder composes three fixed contracts behind one public algorithm surface.

title: Arbitrary-syndrome OSD adapter
description:
Provide the separate parity-check-domain OSD adapter required for BP post-processing and downstream quantum-LDPC decoding.

## Background

The adapter shares the elimination, reliability, and candidate-search engine with generator-matrix OSD but operates in the error domain for an arbitrary target syndrome. It does not reinterpret the codeword-domain adapter.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Accepts a parity-check matrix, target syndrome, and finite bit LLRs and returns an error pattern satisfying $\mathbf{H}\mathbf{e}^{\mathsf T}=\mathbf{s}$ when a candidate is found.
- [hard] REQ-02: Handles zero and nonzero syndromes without requiring a generator matrix or assuming a codeword target.
- [hard] REQ-03: Reuses the shared OSD engine and reports the same rank, candidate, budget, and termination metadata.
- [hard] REQ-04: Matches exhaustive error-pattern search on bounded parity-check fixtures and reports unsatisfied or exhausted searches explicitly.

planning.outcome: A parity-check-domain adapter reuses the OSD engine to solve arbitrary syndromes with deterministic candidate metadata.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The adapter adds one error-domain semantic boundary over the existing engine.

title: LDPC posterior LLR access
description:
Expose the final BP beliefs through a read-only public `LdpcDecoder` API suitable for post-processors.

## Background

`LdpcDecoder` already computes posterior `Llr` values that drive its hard codeword, but the belief vector is private. The accessor follows the `posterior-llr-access` lifecycle contract without exposing mutable decoder internals.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Returns one posterior `Llr` per variable after `decode_to_codeword` and `decode_iterative`.
- [hard] REQ-02: Returns values whose hard decisions exactly match the decoder's final hard codeword.
- [hard] REQ-03: Documents and tests behavior before the first decode and after `reset`.
- [hard] REQ-04: Exposes no mutable access and preserves existing BP convergence and syndrome behavior.

planning.outcome: LdpcDecoder exposes the latest posterior belief slice with documented decode-lifecycle semantics.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The task exposes one existing state vector through a read-only contract.

title: BP fallback OSD decoder
description:
Compose LDPC belief propagation with syndrome-guided OSD as a reusable soft decoder.

## Background

BP remains the first stage. Only a failed syndrome check activates OSD, which consumes the final posterior LLRs and the failed word's syndrome through the parity-check-domain adapter.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Implements `SoftDecoder` and returns the BP decision without invoking OSD when BP passes its syndrome check.
- [hard] REQ-02: Invokes syndrome-guided OSD on BP syndrome failure using the final posterior LLRs and returns a valid corrected decision when found.
- [hard] REQ-03: A composition-specific result records the deciding stage, BP iteration count, OSD candidate count, final syndrome status, and termination reason.
- [hard] REQ-04: Fast-tier tests on a bounded in-tree LDPC fixture deterministically exercise BP-only and OSD-fallback decisions.
- [hard] REQ-05: Repeated seeded inputs produce identical decisions and stage metadata after decoder reset.

planning.outcome: The composed SoftDecoder invokes syndrome-guided OSD only after BP failure and reports stage-specific work metadata.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The composition joins two finished adapters behind one observable fallback policy.

title: Seeded eBCH OSD campaign executable
description:
Add the `gf2-sim` campaign executable for the pinned eBCH OSD reproduction protocol.

## Background

The executable follows the seeded checkpoint and README-provenance conventions of existing `gf2-sim` campaigns. It does not extend the legacy `gf2-coding` TOML registry.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Runs BI-AWGN/BPSK eBCH $(128,64)$ BLER cells versus $E_b/N_0$ for OSD order 2 with order 1 as a separately identified control.
- [hard] REQ-02: Derives deterministic per-cell seeds, checkpoints completed cells, and resumes without repeating completed work.
- [hard] REQ-03: Emits committed-schema JSON with per-point sample and failure counts, binomial confidence intervals, OSD elimination and candidate counters, configuration identity, and runtime-observed provenance.
- [hard] REQ-04: Handles bounded budgets and cancellation with durable partial progress and explicit termination status.
- [hard] REQ-05: Fast deterministic fixtures verify seed stability, resume identity, schema fields, interval computation, and order separation without asserting a statistical curve.

planning.outcome: The gf2-sim executable emits resumable seeded BLER receipts with binomial intervals and runtime-observed provenance.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The executable realizes one pinned campaign protocol with bounded fixture coverage.

title: eBCH OSD curve reproduction
description:
Run the pinned eBCH OSD protocol and commit the evidence for the near-ML reproduction claim.

## Background

This is a seeded, resumable research campaign rather than a fast-tier statistical test. Its order-2 results are compared with the pinned Fossorier1995 curve and interpreted with the Yue2022 cross-check.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Commits the complete JSON receipt for the selected eBCH $(128,64)$ BI-AWGN/BPSK $E_b/N_0$ grid with order-2 and order-1 series.
- [hard] REQ-02: Reports sample count, block-error count, BLER, and binomial confidence interval at each simulated point.
- [hard] REQ-03: Shows that each matched order-2 BLER agrees with the digitized published curve within the recorded confidence interval and digitization precision.
- [hard] REQ-04: Records seeds, git revision, behavioral identity, hardware, toolchain, invocation, checkpoint lineage, and resumption instructions in JSON and README provenance.
- [hard] REQ-05: Preserves any contradictory point and states the resulting falsification instead of omitting or silently rerunning it.

planning.outcome: A committed campaign receipt tests order-2 BLER overlap with the pinned Fossorier1995 curve at stated confidence.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The run executes one pinned protocol and reviews one committed evidence set.

title: OSD pattern-budget variants
description:
Layer bounded pattern segmentation and discarding thresholds on the OSD engine's existing budget metadata.

## Background

The variants are optional complexity controls outside the hard-criterion critical path. GRAND's logistic-weight iterator remains a named semantic exception and is not merged into this Hamming-weight search.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Provides configurable deterministic pattern segmentation and reliability-based discarding thresholds without changing the default exhaustive order-$m$ behavior.
- [hard] REQ-02: Preserves the baseline selected candidate when segmentation is exhaustive and discarding is disabled.
- [hard] REQ-03: Never exceeds the configured candidate budget and reports elimination, generated-pattern, tested-pattern, discarded-pattern, and termination counters.
- [hard] REQ-04: Bounded fixtures demonstrate reduced pattern counts under active thresholds and exact counter relationships.

planning.outcome: Segmented pattern search applies configured discard thresholds while reporting elimination and candidate counters.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The optional policy layer has one bounded counter-based verification surface.
